Figure 25.3 Vitamin D Synthesis and Metabolism
Vitamin D can be obtained in the diet or synthesized when 
skin is exposed to ultraviolet light. Cholecalciferol and 
ergocalciferol must then be changed into their biologically 
active forms by having added to them two hydroxyl (OR) 
groups, in a process known as hydroxylation. The ﬁ rst 
hydroxylation occurs in the liver and the second occurs 
in the kidneys, resulting in 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol, 
the active form of vitamin D
